Package org.apache.juneau.rest.client.mcp.auth

package org.apache.juneau.rest.client.mcp.auth
Client-side OAuth 2.1 token acquisition for the Model Context Protocol 2026-07-28 revision.

This module supplies the token-provider implementations that plug into the McpAuthInterceptor seam of juneau-rest-client-mcp (its Supplier<String>). It deliberately does not depend on juneau-rest-server — the client-side flow/discovery helpers are relocated (see the flow and oidc sub-packages) rather than reused from juneau-rest-server-auth-oauth, which compile-depends on the server. Sub-project D (auth-module de-layering) is expected to later rationalize this relocation.

What's here (F1)
  • McpTokenProvider — a Supplier<String> token manager for pre-provisioned (static) tokens, the client-credentials grant, and the refresh-token grant (SEP-2207, with rotated-refresh-token capture); all requests carry the RFC 8707 resource indicator.
  • McpProtectedResourceMetadataClient and WwwAuthenticateChallenge — the client half of the OAuth 2.1 baseline: consume a 401 WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata pointer, fetch the RFC 9728 PRM document, select an authorization server, and validate its issuer via RFC 8414 / OIDC discovery.
  • McpAuthorizationCodeAcquirer and LoopbackRedirectReceiver — interactive authorization-code + PKCE (S256) acquisition over a loopback redirect for headless/CLI use, including the SEP-2468 iss check on the callback.

Adoption-focused documentation for this module is intentionally tracked as a separate follow-up (not part of F1).

    McpScopeAccumulator
    Computes and tracks the SEP-2350 step-up scope union — the set of scopes a client re-authorizes with after a server emits a per-operation insufficient_scope challenge.
    McpStepUpAuthorizer
    Client-side SEP-2350 step-up state machine: wraps an MCP call so that, on a 401/403 insufficient_scope challenge, it computes the required-scope union (McpScopeAccumulator), drives (re-)authorization via a caller-supplied McpStepUpAuthorizer.Reauthorizer, and retries the original call — bounded by a hard attempt cap with per-(resource, operation) attempt tracking so a misconfigured server can't drive an unbounded re-authorization loop (spec "no more than a few times").

    Builder.
